items: Stream tokens to the client over SSE as they are generated, so time-to-first-token stays low.
Put a queue in front of the GPU pool: absorbs bursts, enables priority for paid tiers, batching, and admission control (429 when full).
Workers write tokens into a Redis Stream keyed by message_id; SSE servers read from it.
Why a queue before GPUs?
Scarce and expensive capacity: queueing gives backpressure, priority, fairness, and batching.
Client disconnects?
Generation continues; tokens are buffered in the stream; resume with Last-Event-ID.
Long context?
Load recent messages; summarize or truncate to fit the window; cache hot conversations.
Cost control?
Per-user rate limits and token quotas at the gateway.
Holding a synchronous connection through the load balancer straight to a GPU.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
Ignoring retries, timeouts and crashes.
